therapeutic_hypothesis.intended_biology: androgen signaling suppression / tumor growth inhibition
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: overall survival (OS) from randomization until death from any cause

biomarker_changes: PSA progression used as component of CRPC definition; darolutamide arm had significantly fewer CRPC events (HR 0.357)
subgroup_findings: Time to CRPC: HR 0.357 (95% CI: 0.302–0.421), p<0.0001; median not reached vs 19.1 months
Time to pain progression: HR 0.792 (95% CI: 0.660–0.950), p=0.0058
Time to subsequent antineoplastic therapy: HR 0.388 (95% CI: 0.328–0.458), p<0.0001
Time to opioid use ≥7 consecutive days: HR 0.688 (95% CI: 0.523–0.906), p=0.0037
Time to worsening of disease-related physical symptoms: HR 1.043 (95% CI: 0.894–1.217), p=0.7073 (not significant)
safety_signals: Any TEAE: 649/652 darolutamide arm vs 643/650 placebo arm
TEAE leading to study drug dose modification: 172 darolutamide vs 112 placebo
TEAE leading to permanent discontinuation of study drug: 90 darolutamide vs 69 placebo
Study drug-related TEAE: 344 darolutamide vs 309 placebo
Febrile neutropenia was the most common serious AE (40 darolutamide vs 39 placebo)

dose_info.dose: 600 mg (2 tablets of 300 mg) twice daily (total 1200 mg/day)
dose_info.dose_modifications: TEAE leading to study drug dose modification: 172 darolutamide arm vs 112 placebo arm

adverse_events.term: TEAE leading to permanent discontinuation of study drug

context.duration: approximately 59 months (primary analysis cut-off); final completion approximately 77 months

modulation_entries.hypothesis: Darolutamide's androgen receptor blockade suppresses AR-driven survival pathways, sensitizing tumor cells to docetaxel-induced mitotic arrest and enhancing overall anti-tumor efficacy beyond docetaxel alone
modulation_entries.citation: HR 0.675 (95% CI: 0.568–0.801), p<0.0001 for OS; the darolutamide + docetaxel arm showed significantly improved OS compared to placebo + docetaxel, with median OS not reached vs 48.9 months

modulation_entries.hypothesis: Docetaxel-induced cytotoxic cell kill complements darolutamide's androgen receptor blockade, reducing tumor burden and delaying castration resistance beyond what AR antagonism alone achieves
modulation_entries.citation: Time to CRPC HR 0.357 (95% CI: 0.302–0.421), p<0.0001; median not reached in darolutamide arm vs 19.1 months in placebo arm, suggesting the combination substantially delays castration resistance
